topics.topic: Whether the multipart body must end after the file part and how any third part or epilogue is handled
questions: Must the multipart body end after the file part, and what happens if a valid third part or epilogue follows it?

quotes:
`UploadBody`'s one implementation is
  `MultipartFileBody(stream, delimiter)`, `policy`, owned by
  `upload_framing`: it gives the file part's bytes and ends before the
  delimiter, holding in memory no more than the delimiter's length of
  look-ahead, so `_parse_export` still receives the bare JSON object.

The declared length `_read_bounded`
  compares is the file part's, so a file of exactly 50 MB is read (A19 rule
  4's required test); a body with an epilogue after the closing delimiter
  declares more than its file, and only a file that near the limit is then
  refused early. The bytes are counted over the file part as it is read.
judgement.why: State 6 makes the file stream stop at the delimiter before any third part and counts only file-part bytes, while trailing content merely inflates the declared-length estimate and causes early refusal only when the file is near the limit.
